answer: A reputation graph that ages like a nebula condensing into stars resists sybils better than any identity check. Every completed job leaves a signed attestation linking agent, client and outcome, so trust accrues only through real work over time. A fresh identity starts hollow: no history, no credit, no access to high-value tasks. An attacker can spawn a comet swarm of new agents overnight, but each must grind through months of low-paid verified work before earning anything worth stealing, while faking that history costs more than the attack can earn.
